previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and gastroparesis was admitted for severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia with a glucose over 1300 mg/dL, diagnosed as hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state. She was treated in the MICU with IV fluids and an insulin drip, which was later transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. Her potassium was elevated at 7.6 and managed with medication. She experienced fluctuating glucose levels, requiring multiple insulin dose adjustments. Her blood pressure, initially in the 190s, improved with labetalol titration to 600 mg TID. A chest X-ray showed pulmonary edema, likely due to fluid overload and hyperglycemia, which resolved with treatment. She underwent successful placement of a left internal jugular port-a-cath due to chronic IV access difficulties. Her gastroparesis symptoms resolved with supportive care, and she tolerated oral intake. She was discharged home with updated insulin regimen, continued antihypertensives, and instructions to follow up with her endocrinologist.
problems: Diabetes with hyperosmolarity, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease

Brief Hospital Course:
___ F w/ DM1, ESRD on ___ HD, diabetic gastroparesis who 
presented after episode of AMS found to be hypothermic and 
hypoglycemic with BG of 25.  

# Hypoglycemic epsiode: After missing a dialysis session, 
___ mother found her with AMS in the setting of 
hypothermia and hypoglycemia (BG 25). Her hypogylcemia quickly 
resolved following administration of glucagon. At baseline she 
is followed by ___ with known brittle type I DM. Pt reported 
decreased PO intake with continued long-acting insulin over the 
course of the day on ___, which likely precipitated the 
hypoglycemia. No recent changes had been made to her insulin 
regimen. On admission she resumed her regular diet and was 
restarted on her home insulin regimen. No further episodes of 
hypoglycemia occurred (in fact she was hyperglycemic, as below). 
___ was consulted and followed while inpatient. Pt was 
educated regarding danger signs of hypoglycemia prior to 
discharge on her current home insulin regimen. She has a 
follow-up appointment scheduled with ___. 

# Abdominal pain/anorexia: Pt reported crampy abdominal pain and 
nausea on the day prior to admission with decreased oral intake. 
She initially reported mild abdominal pain in the ED, however 
she noted that the pain was consistent with her typical 
discomfort from gastroparesis. Reported several episodes of 
loose stools on the day prior to discharge that spontaneously 
resolved. Etiology of symptoms remains unclear, possibly due to 
viral gastroenteritis or related to chronic gastroparesis. No 
sick contacts or recent travel. She remained afebrile, without 
nausea or vomiting. Exam remained benign and WBC within normal 
limits. Home zofran and metoclopramide were continued on 
discharge. 

# Type I DM/Hyperglycemia: History of brittle type I DM, 
complicated by nephropathy and gastroparesis, most recent Hgb 
A1c of 9.0 in ___. Variable blood glucose control recently 
with admission in ___ for hyperglycemia, and hypoglycemic 
episode prompting current admission. On arrival BG initially in 
200's with several spikes up to 400. Home glargine (8U qAM, 10U 
qPM) and home SSI were restarted after she began to take PO. BG 
readings in high 100's-mid ___ prior to discharge. No evidence 
of acute infection in work-up. ___ consulted, recommended 
remaining on current home regimen, which she should continue 
following discharge.   
 
# ESRD: Receives dialysis ___ at baseline. She missed 
dialysis session on ___, received dialysis on ___ and ___ 
while inpatient. Her CKD is due to long-standing type I DM. 
Electrolyte abnormalities corrected with dialysis. Pt was 
continued home home regimen of lasix 40mg daily, calcium 
carbonate, sevelamer carbonate and nephrocaps.  
 
# Hypertension: Pt was hypertensive to SBP 180's on arrival to 
ED and remained hypertensive mostly with SBP 150's-160's during 
admission. This was most likely due to hypervolemia given her 
renal dysfunction and improved following dialysis. Her home 
labetalol 600mg TID was continued.  
 
# Chronic low back pain: Pt reports chronic back pain since MVA. 
She is not on chronic pain medication for this at home. Pt 
complained of back pain several times during this admission and 
was treated with tylenol.   
 
# Chronic normocytic anemia: Hgb 9.9 on admission, remained 
within range of baseline (___) during hospitalization. Most 
likely due to CKD.

consolidation. No acute osseous abnormality is detected.
